title: Why Is the Sea Salty? 🌊 Fun Facts for Kids
description:
The salt in the sea comes from rocks! Leo asks, big sister Mia explains how rain and rivers carry salt to the sea, in under a minute.

Curio Kids Club: short, curious answers to kids' big questions. Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@CurioKidsClub

lines.text: Mia, why is the sea salty?
It starts with rain! When rain falls on land, it slowly washes teeny bits of salt out of rocks and soil.

board.sub: Picks up tiny bits of salt

lines.text: Tiny bits, yes! Then rivers carry that salt all the way down to the sea.

board.text: Rivers carry it to the sea

lines.text: But river water doesn't taste salty.
Right! Each river only carries a teeny bit, too little to taste. But in the sea, it keeps adding up.
Why doesn't the salt leave the sea again?
The sun warms the sea, and water floats up into the air to make clouds. But the salt can't float up. It stays behind!
Then the clouds rain again, more salt washes down, and round and round it goes, for a very, very long time.
So that's why rain isn't salty, but the sea is!
Yep! Rain is fresh water. And some salty stuff also comes from cracks deep under the sea floor.
Rain washes salt from rocks, rivers carry it, and the salt stays in the sea!
That's it! Follow Curio Kids Club for more wonders. And next time someone asks... why is the sea salty?
